Expand private comparison/authority helpers consistently. Ordinary tracking must not enable the runner; core must gain no normal geometry dependency. Review the existing reciprocal feature/dev-dependency edges separately from runtime type identity.

2. **Keep callbacks trusted and narrow.** Invoke the observer factory once with the actual fixture stop; publish one immutable original context and revalidate it through the existing gate. Stage callbacks must run outside channel/binding locks and accept only stage identifiers. They must not choose accounts, recurse into the runner, or perform decoder work. Arbitrary Rust closures are not mechanically bounded merely because the fixture is fixed; document that trust boundary.

3. **Capture before fault injection.** Construct the actual funded `OwnedResourceContext` while channels are healthy, then retain that observer across fresh work. Creating it after cancellation, or checking it before establishing retained `F`, can propagate cancellation early and exercise a different case. Include existing-authority and existing-observer faults with explicitly stated expected outcomes.

4. **Make lifetime assertions possible.** Distinguish container backing, gate metadata, observer metadata, and Weak-only retention. Final pool-release assertions must occur after dropping every account/context/observer clone, including callback captures. Usage snapshots alone do not prove Global-free-before-refund ordering; retain the existing storage instrumentation for that contract.

5. **Keep exposure and limits test-only.** Return bounded scalar reports, no owner/decoder/gate/allocator capabilities. Keep Budget/Resources, four-gate quota, and sixteen-frame/ancestor limits confined to test support. Split fixture-only helpers rather than adding broad dead-code allowances; respect the 400-line module and 150-line function ratchets.

The account, observer, and binding-admission error paths now run `self.record(...)` before stopping the new authority. This removes the reported counterexample: a clean fresh epoch can no longer acquire account `Cancelled` before retained source fault `F` is selected.

The [regression:72](/home/louistrue/.t3/worktrees/ifc-lite/t3-361487a2/rust/core/src/source_resources/observer_tests.rs:72) covers both healthy and independently cancelled accounts. It asserts no operation entry; returned, retained-source, observer, and fresh-source faults all equal `F`; and independent account cancellation remains unchanged. This does not establish universal agreement between epochs already independently stopped with different faults: their first faults remain irreversible. That case needs an explicit expected-precedence assertion in future coverage, rather than assuming every channel can be rewritten to `F`.

**Proposed test-design verdict: suitable for implementation with these concrete constraints.**

1. **Preserve the feature boundary.** Compile the same private implementation under `all(source-resource-tracking, any(test, source-resource-gate-test-support))`. Expand private comparison/authority helpers consistently. Ordinary tracking must not enable the runner; core must gain no normal geometry dependency. Review the existing reciprocal feature/dev-dependency edges separately from runtime type identity.

2. **Keep callbacks trusted and narrow.** Invoke the observer factory once with the actual fixture stop; publish one immutable original context and revalidate it through the existing gate. Stage callbacks must run outside channel/binding locks and accept only stage identifiers. They must not choose accounts, recurse into the runner, or perform decoder work. Arbitrary Rust closures are not mechanically bounded merely because the fixture is fixed; document that trust boundary.

3. **Capture before fault injection.** Construct the actual funded `OwnedResourceContext` while channels are healthy, then retain that observer across fresh work. Creating it after cancellation, or checking it before establishing retained `F`, can propagate cancellation early and exercise a different case. Include existing-authority and existing-observer faults with explicitly stated expected outcomes.

4. **Make lifetime assertions possible.** Distinguish container backing, gate metadata, observer metadata, and Weak-only retention. Final pool-release assertions must occur after dropping every account/context/observer clone, including callback captures. Usage snapshots alone do not prove Global-free-before-refund ordering; retain the existing storage instrumentation for that contract.

5. **Keep exposure and limits test-only.** Return bounded scalar reports, no owner/decoder/gate/allocator capabilities. Keep Budget/Resources, four-gate quota, and sixteen-frame/ancestor limits confined to test support. Split fixture-only helpers rather than adding broad dead-code allowances; respect the 400-line module and 150-line function ratchets.
